questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: The nurse reviews Diphenhydramine on a medication list. Which drug class should the nurse identify?

options.text: First-generation H1 antihistamine
Second-generation H1 antihistamine
Opioid antitussive
Nonopioid antitussive

questions.rationale: Diphenhydramine is the listed prototype for First-generation H1 antihistamine.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which action explains the therapeutic effect of Diphenhydramine?

options.text: Blocks H1 receptors and crosses the blood-brain barrier
Stimulates beta2 receptors to relax bronchial smooth muscle
Inhibits acetylcholinesterase to increase acetylcholine
Suppresses cough through opioid receptors

questions.rationale: Blocks H1 receptors and crosses the blood-brain barrier. This is the action described in the course medication review.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client becomes sleepy after taking diphenhydramine. Which explanation best fits this response?

options.text: The medication enters the CNS and can cause sedation
It is a rescue bronchodilator producing an expected therapeutic response
Sedation establishes that the client has developed serotonin syndrome
First-generation antihistamines cannot affect alertness

questions.rationale: Diphenhydramine crosses the blood-brain barrier and commonly causes drowsiness.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client starting diphenhydramine plans to drive to work. Which teaching is most appropriate?

options.text: Avoid driving until the medication's effects on alertness are known
Take an extra dose before driving to reduce allergy distraction
Alcohol can be used to counteract drowsiness
Driving safety is unaffected by this medication

questions.rationale: Sedation can impair driving and other activities requiring alertness.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which finding in a client taking diphenhydramine is consistent with an anticholinergic effect?

options.text: Difficulty emptying the bladder
Profuse salivation
Frequent watery stools
A marked increase in sweating as the intended effect

questions.rationale: Urinary retention is among the anticholinergic effects of diphenhydramine.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: An older adult reports dizziness after diphenhydramine. Which nursing concern has priority in the care plan?

options.text: Risk for falls
Need to encourage unassisted stair climbing
Expected improvement in balance
Need to double the next dose

questions.rationale: Sedation and impaired alertness increase fall risk, especially in older adults.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client taking diphenhydramine reports dry mouth. Which suggestion matches the course teaching?

options.text: Use sugarless gum or hard candy if safe to swallow
Restrict all fluids regardless of health status
Add another sedating antihistamine
Take alcohol with each dose

questions.rationale: Sugarless gum or hard candy can help manage medication-related dry mouth.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which over-the-counter product should a client taking diphenhydramine discuss with the nurse before combining them?

options.text: A nighttime product that also causes drowsiness
A saline nasal spray without other active ingredients
An oral rehydration product alone
A plain skin moisturizer

questions.rationale: Combining CNS depressants can increase sedation; active ingredients should be reviewed.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client taking diphenhydramine develops constipation and blurred vision. How should these findings be interpreted?

options.text: They can reflect the medication's anticholinergic activity
They prove the medication is a beta2 agonist
They are the desired endpoints of allergy therapy
They exclude a medication effect

questions.rationale: Constipation and blurred vision are anticholinergic effects, not treatment goals.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which client statement about diphenhydramine requires correction?

options.text: I can drink alcohol because this allergy medication does not affect the brain
I will watch for unusual drowsiness
I will report trouble urinating
I will use caution with activities requiring balance

questions.rationale: Diphenhydramine enters the CNS; alcohol can worsen its sedative effects.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: The nurse reviews Cetirizine on a medication list. Which drug class should the nurse identify?

options.text: Second-generation H1 antihistamine
First-generation H1 antihistamine
Opioid antitussive
Nonopioid antitussive

questions.rationale: Cetirizine is the listed prototype for Second-generation H1 antihistamine.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which action explains the therapeutic effect of Cetirizine?

options.text: Blocks peripheral H1 receptors with less CNS penetration than first-generation agents
Activates opioid receptors in the cough center
Blocks leukotriene receptors in the airways
Stimulates muscarinic receptors to increase secretions

questions.rationale: Blocks peripheral H1 receptors with less CNS penetration than first-generation agents. This is the action described in the course medication review.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client needs allergy relief during the workday and experienced pronounced sleepiness with diphenhydramine. Which feature supports discussing cetirizine?

options.text: It is generally less sedating than first-generation antihistamines
It reliably provides immediate relief of severe bronchospasm
It treats cough by an opioid mechanism
It increases dopamine in the brain

questions.rationale: Cetirizine has less CNS penetration and is generally less sedating.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which symptom is an appropriate target when cetirizine is prescribed for seasonal allergies?

options.text: Histamine-mediated allergy symptoms
An active generalized seizure
An acute Parkinsonian wearing-off episode
An episode of lithium toxicity

questions.rationale: Cetirizine is an antihistamine used for allergy symptom control.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client says cetirizine can never cause drowsiness. Which response is best?

options.text: It is less likely to cause drowsiness, but individual responses still need monitoring
No monitoring is needed because it cannot affect alertness
It causes the same severe sedation in every client
Drowsiness proves that the medication is an opioid

questions.rationale: Less sedation does not mean that every client will remain fully alert.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which comparison between cetirizine and diphenhydramine is accurate?

options.text: Cetirizine crosses the blood-brain barrier less readily
Cetirizine is an opioid whereas diphenhydramine is not
Cetirizine is a rescue inhaler whereas diphenhydramine is a controller
Cetirizine has greater expected CNS sedation in every client

questions.rationale: The course review distinguishes second-generation agents by reduced CNS penetration.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client with seasonal allergies asks whether cetirizine will stop a sudden asthma attack. Which response is appropriate?

options.text: It treats allergy symptoms and does not replace the prescribed rescue bronchodilator
It is the preferred immediate rescue treatment
Its main action is rapid beta2 stimulation
An extra tablet should replace the rescue inhaler

questions.rationale: Cetirizine blocks histamine; it is not a rescue bronchodilator.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which finding would best indicate that cetirizine is achieving the intended allergy benefit?

options.text: Reduced bothersome allergy symptoms with preserved daytime function
Profound sedation that prevents normal activity
Increasing wheezing during an acute attack
New inability to empty the bladder

questions.rationale: Symptom relief, rather than sedation or urinary retention, is the treatment goal.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client changes from diphenhydramine to cetirizine and asks why the drugs differ in sedation. Which factor is most relevant?

options.text: The extent to which the drug reaches CNS histamine receptors
Whether the drug is inhaled into a dialysis cartridge
Whether the drug is a long-acting beta2 agonist
The number of opioid receptors in the medulla

questions.rationale: Reduced blood-brain barrier penetration helps explain less sedation with cetirizine.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which client plan after starting cetirizine reflects appropriate caution?

options.text: Observe personal alertness before driving or operating equipment
Assume all second-generation antihistamines are completely free of adverse effects
Take diphenhydramine with every dose without checking
Use it instead of all prescribed asthma medications

questions.rationale: Even less-sedating agents warrant attention to individual response and medication combinations.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: The nurse reviews Codeine on a medication list. Which drug class should the nurse identify?

options.text: Opioid antitussive
First-generation H1 antihistamine
Second-generation H1 antihistamine
Nonopioid antitussive

questions.rationale: Codeine is the listed prototype for Opioid antitussive.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which action explains the therapeutic effect of Codeine?

options.text: Suppresses the cough reflex through the medullary cough center
Blocks peripheral H1 receptors without a central cough effect
Stimulates beta2 receptors to open the airways
Inhibits leukotriene receptors to reduce inflammation

questions.rationale: Suppresses the cough reflex through the medullary cough center. This is the action described in the course medication review.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which assessment is especially important before administering codeine for cough?

options.text: Respiratory rate and breathing quality
Only the client's hair color
Only the size of the inhaler spacer
The presence of oral thrush as the sole assessment

questions.rationale: Codeine can cause respiratory depression and requires respiratory assessment.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client receiving codeine is difficult to arouse and breathing slowly. What is the nurse's priority?

options.text: Promptly assess breathing and follow the emergency and medication-hold protocol
Give the next dose early to reduce coughing
Encourage the client to sleep without assessment
Treat the change as evidence of effective allergy control

questions.rationale: Reduced alertness with slow breathing can signal opioid-related respiratory depression.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which teaching helps a client manage constipation associated with codeine when not otherwise restricted?

options.text: Maintain appropriate fluid and fiber intake
Restrict fluids to prevent all bowel movements
Take an additional opioid with each meal
Ignore persistent constipation

questions.rationale: The course review recommends fluid and fiber to help prevent opioid-related constipation.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client feels lightheaded when standing after codeine. Which instruction is appropriate?

options.text: Change positions slowly and obtain help if unsteady
Stand abruptly to build tolerance
Take alcohol to improve balance
Skip assessment because opioids cannot cause lightheadedness

questions.rationale: Codeine may cause lightheadedness; slow position changes reduce fall risk.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which client statement about codeine needs follow-up?

options.text: I will combine it with alcohol to sleep through the cough
I will watch for unusual sleepiness
I will report slowed breathing
I will review other sedating medicines with the nurse

questions.rationale: Alcohol and other CNS depressants can increase opioid sedation and respiratory risk.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client asks why codeine reduced a dry cough without opening narrowed bronchi. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Its antitussive action suppresses the central cough reflex
It is a short-acting beta2 agonist
It dissolves mucus by directly increasing airway inflammation
It is an inhaled muscarinic antagonist

questions.rationale: Codeine suppresses cough centrally; cough suppression is different from bronchodilation.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which finding is more concerning than uncomplicated constipation in a client taking codeine?

options.text: New shallow, slowed respirations
Mild reduction in cough frequency
A request for advice on fiber intake
A report that the prescribed dose relieved cough

questions.rationale: Respiratory depression can be immediately dangerous and takes priority over routine constipation teaching.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A nurse evaluates a client's response to prescribed codeine for cough. Which finding supports therapeutic benefit without an obvious safety warning?

options.text: Less coughing while remaining readily arousable with adequate breathing
No cough because the client is unresponsive with shallow breathing
Increasing sedation accompanied by declining respirations
Severe lightheadedness when attempting to stand

questions.rationale: Cough relief must be evaluated together with alertness and respiratory safety.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: The nurse reviews Dextromethorphan on a medication list. Which drug class should the nurse identify?

options.text: Nonopioid antitussive
First-generation H1 antihistamine
Second-generation H1 antihistamine
Opioid antitussive

questions.rationale: Dextromethorphan is the listed prototype for Nonopioid antitussive.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which action explains the therapeutic effect of Dextromethorphan?

options.text: Acts on the medullary cough center to suppress cough without opioid analgesic properties
Selectively stimulates beta2 receptors for rapid bronchodilation
Replaces missing dopamine in the brain
Blocks peripheral muscarinic receptors for long-acting bronchodilation

questions.rationale: Acts on the medullary cough center to suppress cough without opioid analgesic properties. This is the action described in the course medication review.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client asks whether dextromethorphan is the same type of cough medicine as codeine. Which response is correct?

options.text: Dextromethorphan is a nonopioid antitussive
Both drugs are inhaled corticosteroids
Dextromethorphan is a long-acting opioid analgesic
Both drugs primarily treat histamine-mediated sneezing

questions.rationale: The prototype list identifies dextromethorphan as nonopioid and codeine as opioid.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which symptom should the nurse evaluate for improvement after prescribed dextromethorphan?

options.text: Bothersome cough frequency
Muscle rigidity from Parkinson disease
An ongoing seizure
Metabolic syndrome

questions.rationale: Dextromethorphan suppresses the cough reflex.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client reports dizziness after dextromethorphan. Which teaching is appropriate?

options.text: Use caution with driving and activities requiring alertness
Drive immediately because nonopioid drugs never impair alertness
Take extra doses to overcome dizziness
Add alcohol to prevent nausea

questions.rationale: Dizziness and drowsiness are possible even though the drug is nonopioid.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client taking dextromethorphan reports a persistent cough for more than a week and a high fever. What should the nurse recommend?

options.text: Contact the provider for evaluation
Continue increasing the dose without assessment
Assume fever demonstrates the drug is working
Replace all prescribed respiratory treatments with the syrup

questions.rationale: The course review identifies persistent cough or high fever as reasons to seek follow-up.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which adverse effect is listed for dextromethorphan in the medication review?

options.text: Nausea or gastrointestinal upset
Gingival hyperplasia as its defining effect
Lithium toxicity
Tardive dyskinesia as its routine effect

questions.rationale: Gastrointestinal upset and nausea are recognized adverse effects in the review.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client asks whether dextromethorphan should be used for pain relief. Which response is accurate?

options.text: It suppresses cough and lacks the opioid analgesic action described for opioid medicines
It is prescribed primarily to relieve severe pain
It restores acetylcholine in Alzheimer disease
It is a maintenance bronchodilator

questions.rationale: The course review distinguishes cough suppression from opioid analgesia.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which statement indicates that teaching about dextromethorphan was understood?

options.text: Nonopioid does not mean I should exceed the prescribed or labeled dose
I can double every dose because it is not an opioid
It should replace my rescue inhaler during sudden wheezing
Dizziness means I must take the medication more frequently

questions.rationale: The nonopioid classification does not eliminate adverse effects or the need to follow dosing instructions.

questions.topic: Medications for the Upper Respiratory System
questions.stem: For a client prescribed Dextromethorphan, a client has both cough and sudden wheezing. Which medication distinction should the nurse reinforce?

options.text: Dextromethorphan suppresses cough; it does not substitute for prescribed acute bronchodilation
Dextromethorphan and albuterol have identical primary actions
Cough suppression guarantees that bronchospasm has resolved
A cough syrup is always sufficient for an acute asthma attack

questions.rationale: Central cough suppression is different from rapid relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: The nurse reviews Albuterol on a medication list. Which drug class should the nurse identify?

options.text: SABA
LABA
SAMA
LAMA

questions.rationale: Albuterol is the listed prototype for SABA.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which action explains the therapeutic effect of Albuterol?

options.text: Stimulates beta2 receptors to rapidly relax bronchial smooth muscle
Suppresses airway inflammation through corticosteroid activity
Provides prolonged muscarinic blockade for daily maintenance
Blocks H1 receptors to treat allergies

questions.rationale: Stimulates beta2 receptors to rapidly relax bronchial smooth muscle. This is the action described in the course medication review.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client develops sudden wheezing. Which role does prescribed albuterol have?

options.text: Rapid rescue bronchodilation
Long-term dopamine replacement
Prevention of all future seizures
Treatment of oral candidiasis

questions.rationale: Albuterol is a short-acting rescue bronchodilator.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which finding after albuterol is consistent with an expected adverse effect?

options.text: Tremor and nervousness
Gingival overgrowth
Progressive memory improvement
Painless breast enlargement

questions.rationale: Tremor and nervousness are listed beta-agonist effects.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which vital sign should the nurse monitor during albuterol therapy?

options.text: Heart rate
Temperature as the only relevant vital sign
Pain score as the only relevant measurement
Pupil size as the sole safety measure

questions.rationale: Albuterol can cause tachycardia and palpitations.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client's wheezing decreases after albuterol. Which explanation supports this improvement?

options.text: Bronchial smooth muscle has relaxed
The medication immediately removed all airway infection
It replaced an inhaled corticosteroid's anti-inflammatory action
It suppressed the medullary cough center as an opioid

questions.rationale: Beta2 stimulation produces bronchodilation.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which client statement about albuterol needs correction?

options.text: It is the same type of long-term anti-inflammatory medicine as fluticasone
I should learn correct inhaler technique
My pulse may increase after a dose
I should follow my prescribed rescue plan

questions.rationale: Albuterol provides rapid bronchodilation; fluticasone reduces inflammation.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client reports a pounding heartbeat after albuterol. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Assess the heart rate and symptoms
Ignore it because albuterol cannot affect pulse
Give extra unscheduled doses
Recommend alcohol to reduce palpitations

questions.rationale: Palpitations warrant assessment because tachycardia can occur.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which instruction is important for effective delivery of albuterol by metered-dose inhaler?

options.text: Demonstrate and check the prescribed inhaler technique
Swallow the medication canister contents
Spray every dose away from the mouth
Use a maintenance capsule by swallowing it instead

questions.rationale: Correct inhaler technique helps medication reach the airways.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client must distinguish albuterol from salmeterol. Which statement is accurate?

options.text: Albuterol is short acting and used for acute symptoms
Albuterol is a long-acting controller that cannot provide rapid relief
Both medicines are opioid cough suppressants
Both are inhaled corticosteroids

questions.rationale: Albuterol is the SABA rescue drug; salmeterol is a LABA maintenance agent.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: The nurse reviews Salmeterol on a medication list. Which drug class should the nurse identify?

options.text: LABA
SABA
SAMA
LAMA

questions.rationale: Salmeterol is the listed prototype for LABA.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which action explains the therapeutic effect of Salmeterol?

options.text: Produces prolonged beta2-receptor stimulation for maintenance bronchodilation
Rapidly reverses every acute asthma attack as the primary rescue drug
Blocks histamine H1 receptors to reduce sneezing
Inhibits acetylcholinesterase in cerebral synapses

questions.rationale: Produces prolonged beta2-receptor stimulation for maintenance bronchodilation. This is the action described in the course medication review.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client plans to use salmeterol for a sudden asthma attack. Which teaching is needed?

options.text: Use the prescribed rescue medicine for acute symptoms; salmeterol is maintenance therapy
Take repeated extra salmeterol doses until relief occurs
Salmeterol is the preferred immediate rescue medicine
Stop the rescue medication because it duplicates all controller effects

questions.rationale: Salmeterol is not intended to relieve acute asthma attacks.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Why is salmeterol often prescribed with an inhaled corticosteroid for asthma?

options.text: The medicines address bronchodilation and airway inflammation
Both medicines are opioid antitussives
The corticosteroid converts salmeterol into a short-acting drug
The combination removes all need for symptom monitoring

questions.rationale: Salmeterol maintains bronchodilation while the corticosteroid treats inflammation.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which adverse effect should the nurse recognize with salmeterol?

options.text: Tachycardia
Gingival hyperplasia
Lithium-related coarse tremor by definition
Oral contraceptive failure as its defining effect

questions.rationale: Tachycardia is among the effects listed for salmeterol.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client feels well on maintenance salmeterol. Which statement shows understanding?

options.text: I will use it as prescribed rather than reserve it only for sudden attacks
I will use it only during severe acute wheezing
I will replace my rescue medicine with extra maintenance doses
I can stop all respiratory follow-up permanently

questions.rationale: Maintenance therapy is scheduled according to the prescribed plan.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which medication should a client identify as the long-acting beta2 agent rather than the short-acting one?

options.text: Salmeterol
Albuterol
Ipratropium
Fluticasone

questions.rationale: Salmeterol is the LABA prototype.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client asks if salmeterol directly replaces a corticosteroid's anti-inflammatory action. Which response is best?

options.text: No; its primary role is prolonged bronchodilation
Yes; it is the same corticosteroid class
Yes; it directly treats oral thrush
No; it is an opioid analgesic

questions.rationale: The drugs have complementary rather than identical primary actions.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which symptoms are listed as possible salmeterol effects?

options.text: Headache and muscle cramps
Gingival overgrowth and jaundice as its routine pair
Urinary incontinence and marked salivation
Progressive bradycardia as its intended outcome

questions.rationale: The review lists headache, nervousness, tachycardia, and muscle cramps.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client using salmeterol reports new acute breathing difficulty. Which response is appropriate?

options.text: Follow the acute rescue plan and seek help as indicated
Assume maintenance therapy guarantees that an attack cannot occur
Use extra doses without following the plan
Wait for several days without assessment

questions.rationale: Maintenance use does not eliminate the need for an acute symptom plan.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: The nurse reviews Ipratropium on a medication list. Which drug class should the nurse identify?

options.text: SAMA
SABA
LABA
LAMA

questions.rationale: Ipratropium is the listed prototype for SAMA.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which action explains the therapeutic effect of Ipratropium?

options.text: Blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors in airway smooth muscle to inhibit bronchoconstriction
Stimulates beta2 receptors as a short-acting agonist
Blocks serotonin reuptake in cerebral synapses
Suppresses immune activity as an inhaled corticosteroid

questions.rationale: Blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors in airway smooth muscle to inhibit bronchoconstriction. This is the action described in the course medication review.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which common complaint is consistent with inhaled ipratropium?

options.text: Dry mouth
Profuse salivation
Gingival hyperplasia
Mania as its intended effect

questions.rationale: Dry mouth is a common anticholinergic effect.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client is prescribed both ipratropium and albuterol. Why might they be used together?

options.text: They produce bronchodilation through different receptor actions
They are identical beta2 agonists
Both are corticosteroids
Ipratropium prevents albuterol from reaching the lungs

questions.rationale: Different mechanisms can provide complementary bronchodilation.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client reports a bitter taste after ipratropium. Which teaching matches the course review?

options.text: Rinse the mouth after use
Stop all airway medications without contacting anyone
Swallow the inhaler capsule
Take an extra dose to remove the taste

questions.rationale: The review recommends rinsing after use to reduce the bitter taste.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which finding should be evaluated as a possible local effect of ipratropium?

options.text: Throat irritation and hoarseness
Blue-green vision as its defining effect
Gingival overgrowth
A new therapeutic increase in dopamine

questions.rationale: Throat irritation and hoarseness are listed effects.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which comparison correctly distinguishes ipratropium from tiotropium?

options.text: Ipratropium is short acting; tiotropium is long acting
Ipratropium is a corticosteroid; tiotropium is an opioid
Both are H1 antihistamines
Tiotropium is a seizure rescue drug

questions.rationale: The prototype document identifies SAMA and LAMA agents separately.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: For a client prescribed Ipratropium, a client asks what muscarinic blockade does in the airways. Which response is accurate?

options.text: It reduces acetylcholine-mediated bronchoconstriction
It increases serotonin reuptake
It converts levodopa to dopamine
It raises acetylcholine at cerebral synapses

questions.rationale: Ipratropium opposes muscarinic effects that narrow the airways.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which response best suggests the intended effect of ipratropium?

options.text: Improved airflow from reduced bronchoconstriction
More severe wheezing
Relief of neuropathic pain as its primary use
Resolution of an active seizure

questions.rationale: Ipratropium is used for bronchodilation, not neurologic indications.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client says dry mouth means ipratropium is treating allergies by blocking H1 receptors. What needs clarification?

options.text: Dry mouth can result from antimuscarinic activity; ipratropium is not an H1 antihistamine
Ipratropium is a first-generation H1 antihistamine
Dry mouth proves serotonin syndrome
All drugs causing dry mouth belong to the same class

questions.rationale: Similar adverse effects can occur across different drug classes.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: The nurse reviews Tiotropium on a medication list. Which drug class should the nurse identify?

options.text: LAMA
SABA
LABA
SAMA

questions.rationale: Tiotropium is the listed prototype for LAMA.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which action explains the therapeutic effect of Tiotropium?

options.text: Provides long-acting muscarinic receptor blockade for maintenance airway treatment
Rapidly stimulates beta2 receptors as a rescue SABA
Inhibits central serotonin reuptake
Blocks peripheral H1 receptors for seasonal allergies

questions.rationale: Provides long-acting muscarinic receptor blockade for maintenance airway treatment. This is the action described in the course medication review.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client receives a tiotropium inhalation capsule for the prescribed device. Which instruction is essential?

options.text: Use the capsule in the inhalation device; do not swallow it
Swallow the capsule with food
Dissolve it in a glass of water and drink it
Chew it to increase absorption

questions.rationale: The review explicitly warns not to swallow inhalation capsules.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client with an enlarged prostate starts tiotropium. Which function warrants monitoring?

options.text: Ability to urinate
Color vision as the sole concern
Gum growth as the main concern
Daily cough suppression by an opioid effect

questions.rationale: Tiotropium can cause urinary retention, especially relevant with BPH.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which complaint is consistent with tiotropium's antimuscarinic effects?

options.text: Constipation and dry mouth
Excess saliva and diarrhea
Serotonin syndrome as its expected therapeutic response
Increased appetite with no other possible effects

questions.rationale: Dry mouth, constipation, and urinary retention are listed effects.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: A client asks whether tiotropium should replace the rescue inhaler during sudden wheezing. Which response is appropriate?

options.text: It is maintenance treatment; follow the prescribed rescue plan for sudden symptoms
Swallow an extra inhalation capsule
Use it as the only immediate rescue treatment
It is identical to albuterol in onset and class

questions.rationale: Tiotropium is a long-acting maintenance antimuscarinic.

questions.topic: Medications for the Lower Respiratory System
questions.stem: Which client statement about tiotropium shows understanding?

options.text: I will use the prescribed device and scheduled maintenance plan
I will swallow all capsules labeled for inhalation
I will stop treatment whenever I have one symptom-free day without guidance
I will take extra doses whenever my mouth feels dry
